newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Commerzbank to extend CZK2bln to Czech Agrobanka.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank to extend CZK2bln to Czech Agrobanka.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG has offered a two-billion crown credit guaranteed by the Czech National Bank (CNB) to Agrobanka, which is under temporary central bank administration, Commerzbank chairman Martin Kohlhaussen said on Tuesday.
When asked at a news conference whether Commerzbank was interested in taking a stake in Agrobanka, Kohlhaussen said "A clear answer is no. There is no interest to invest in Agrobanka."
He gave no details of the terms of the credit.
"We have decided, quite voluntarily, and without being requested to do so, to provide support for Agrobanka," said Kohlhaussen.

"We are making available a credit of two billion crowns which is secured by means of a guarantee from the Czech National Bank. Our offer is intended to show how keen we are that the (Czech) banking system regains its stability."

Kohlhaussen said many poeple were now doubting the rectitude of the market reforms of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's centre-right government but he urged Czech officials to keep a cool head and push on with reform.
"We do not share such doubts. There is no reasonable alternative to the path taken by the Czech Republic up to now," he said.
"If it (the Czech Republic) stays the course without wavering -- and that is what official sources repeatedly claim -- these teething troubles of a market economy system will be overcome, he added."

The Commerzbank chairman said the market would inevitably sift out bad management and unsound companies but reminded politicians and the central bank that they had a role to play in ensuring that problems were not allowed to get out of control.
"Should new crises develop, it is up to them to react promptly, and make sure that they don't spread -- or to ensure that the confidence of Czech and foreign investors is quickly restored."
Agrobanka was put under temporary forced administration by the Czech National Bank in September after running into liquidity problems.
It is the country's fifth largest bank and the largest fully-private Czech bank.
